item.title: STIHL主任:改革的时机——这就是我们如何保持繁荣和福利国家
item.author: Dr. Nikolas Stihl, Chairman of the STIHL Advisory Board and Supervisory Board
item.description:
本地机器翻译 · 原文附后

德国的经济状况是严重的,非常严重的.

在过去的八年里,我们失去了大约15%的工业生产.

月复一日,德国损失了大约15,000个工业工作.

而支撑我们繁荣的工业基础也开始受到侵蚀.

私人净投资已降至近零。

总而言之,公司所做的只不过是替换疲惫不堪的东西。

高成本使公司的投资意愿陷于瘫痪。

甚至德国政府在2025年中期推出的特殊折旧套案("Investitionsbooster")也没有做任何改变.

而支撑我们繁荣的工业基础也开始受到侵蚀.

医生

Nikolas Stihl,STIHL咨询委员会和监督委员会主席

当然,美国的关税、中国的侵略性工业政策以及地缘政治的紧张也给投资带来压力。

但真正的问题是我们自己造成的:经济监管过度,能源成本高,劳动力成本高,税收高,教育和技能水平下降。

计划的改革不足以扭转经济趋势

年初,许多企业家几乎对德国的改革能力失去了信心.

7月,德国政府对法定医疗保险的改革,以及养老金,税收和劳动力市场的改革计划,令大家感到惊讶.

这个一揽子计划不足以使德国摆脱其结构危机.

但是,目前的联盟表明,它可以妥协,帮助推动国家前进。

如果这些妥协现在不挑剔,被淡化,商业对政治信心的破坏将是毁灭性的。

计划中的改革仍然不是我们所希望的突破,那就是真正能扭转经济的突破。

-(c) 施蒂尔

现在,我们需要将一切投入到下一轮的改革中,这些改革为投资和增长带来真正的动力。

这意味着执政联盟、雇主和工会都走出他们的舒适地带,履行他们对德国的责任。

用于国防和基础设施的特别基金很难导致经济的自立上升,除非在这里做生意的条件明显改善。

接下来的改革步骤必须不断削减官僚机构,提高总的工时,降低劳动力成本,并给公司投资研发的真正理由.

接下来的改革步骤必须不断削减官僚机构,提高总的工时,降低劳动力成本,并给公司投资研发的真正理由.

原文：STIHL chief: Time for reforms — this is how we retain prosperity and the welfare state

The state of the German economy is serious, very serious. Over the past eight years, we've lost approximately 15 percent of our industrial production. Month after month, Germany loses around 15,000 industrial jobs. And the industrial base that underpins our prosperity is starting to erode. Private net investment has fallen to almost zero. On balance, companies are doing nothing more than replacing what wears out. High costs are paralyzing companies' willingness to invest. Even the special depreciation package (the "Investitionsbooster") that the German government introduced in mid-2025 has done nothing to change that.

And the industrial base that underpins our prosperity is starting to erode.

Dr. Nikolas Stihl, Chairman of the STIHL Advisory Board and Supervisory Board

Of course, US tariffs, China's aggressive industrial policy, and geopolitical tensions weigh on investment too. But the real problems are of our own making: an overregulated economy, high energy costs, high labor costs, high taxes, and falling levels of education and skills.

Planned reforms are not enough to reverse the economic trend

At the beginning of the year, many entrepreneurs had almost lost faith in Germany's ability to reform. In July, the German government surprised everyone with a reform of statutory health insurance, along with reform plans for pensions, taxes, and the labor market. This package isn't enough to pull Germany out of its structural crisis. But the current coalition showed it can compromise to help move the country forward. If those compromises were now unpicked and watered down, the damage to business confidence in politics would be devastating. The planned reforms are still not the breakthrough we were hoping for, the one that would actually turn the economy around.

XXXX - (c) Stihl

Right now, we need to put everything into the next round of reforms, the ones that deliver real momentum for investment and growth. And that means the governing coalition, employers, and unions all stepping outside their comfort zones to live up to their responsibility for Germany. The special funds for defense and infrastructure will hardly lead to a self-sustaining upswing in the economy unless conditions for doing business here improve noticeably. The next reform steps have to keep cutting bureaucracy, raise the total hours worked, bring labor costs down, and give companies real reasons to invest in research and development.
